text: This document defines the testing requirements for an Open Xhaul transport infrastructure. It is based on Xhaul Transport Requirement document, Packet Switched Architectures and Solutions document, the WDM-based Fronthaul Transport, and Synchronization Architecture and Solution documents. It defines test cases and provides dedicated chapters for different solutions.
trace: 3 Scope

text: This document uses information published by O-RAN, 3GPP, IEEE, ITU-T, IETF, CableLabs, NGMN and several other relevant standard bodies and industry associations. It contains educational, informative, and normative content.
trace: 3 Scope

text: Version 02.00 of this document adds new test cases for synchronization \(9.2\) and WDM \(7.1.5 & 7.1.6\). Version 3.0 adds new test cases for Synchronization \(9.3\) and WDM \(7.1.6\).
trace: 3 Scope

text: What is not covered in this document:
trace: 3 Scope

text: • The document shall minimize any unnecessary overlap with content presented in other O-RAN testing specifications such as WG4 Conformance Test \(S-Plane\) specification. Whereas the latter is about testing an O-RU or O-DU, this document verifies the transport networks placed between those O-RAN components. Some of the presented synchronization test cases may be moved from this document to other documents such as the WG4 Conformance Test specification in agreement with respective authors of the latter document.

text: 6 Test approach and methodology
trace: 6 Test approach and methodology

text: This section provides a definition of test use cases in Open Xhaul transport networks.
trace: 6 Test approach and methodology

text: 6.1System under test
trace: 6.1System under test

text: This specification covers cases that test:
trace: 6.1System under test

text:
* 1\. Xhaul networks from a UNI interface to another UNI interface
  * 2\. Xhaul network segments that carry traffic for an overlay network.
  * 3\. Individual TNEs or their components
trace: 6.1System under test
6.1System under test

text: Figure 6-1: Xhaul Transport Networks
trace: 6.1System under test
6.1System under test
6.1System under test
6.1System under test

text: Figure 6-1 depicts a simplified overview of Xhaul transport networks that are composed of Fronthaul, Midhaul and Backhaul. The first category of test cases covers the network segments between UNI interfaces of Fronthaul, Midhaul or Backhaul. These test cases do not cross the O-DU or O-CU, and remain within the same network \(Fronthaul, Midhaul, or Backhaul\).
trace: 6.1System under test
6.1System under test

text: Beyond these UNI interfaces, there may be other UNI interfaces within the individual Xhaul networks. Figure  6-2 illustrates one use case that includes UNI interfaces within a Fronthaul Network. An example is the use of a WDM physical interface \(layer below\) between packet-based solutions \(layer above\). Other use cases include -but are not limited to- use of wireless, PON, or DOCSIS infrastructure in Backhaul, Midhaul, or Fronthaul if the underlying technologies meet the necessary SLAs.

text: 6.2Testing Parameters
trace: 6.2Testing Parameters

text: The test cases in this specification relate to the metrics listed in existing WG9 requirement and solution documents. Examples include throughput, delay, time error or optical power level.
trace: 6.2Testing Parameters

text: 6.3Testing Methodologies
trace: 6.3Testing Methodologies

text: Test methodologies can be categorized as follows:
trace: 6.3Testing Methodologies

text:
* Equipment level vs. network level test
  * Technology specific test methodologies
trace: 6.3Testing Methodologies
6.3Testing Methodologies

text: The equipment level tests verify the functionality or performance of an individual equipment or its components and are covered in the next section. The network level tests perform tests from a network UNI to another UNI across one or multiple equipment and are described in remaining chapters of this document.
trace: 6.3Testing Methodologies
6.3Testing Methodologies

text: There are technology specification test cases. Optical layer tests perform tests at optical layer, they include power level or wavelength measurements. Packet layer tests use packet-based methods that generate and analyse Ethernet/eCPRI packets. Synchronization tests include measurements of time or frequency error that measure synchronizations signal or PTP timestamps against a reference signal that may be derived from a GNSS receiver. They may need to emulate a PTP timeTransmitter or timeReceiver function to be able to perform these measurements.

text: The STRxs can send the loopback configuration message and receive the response message of the loopback configuration success from the tested optical modules through the in-band OAM channel. The STRxs also can receive the loopback configuration message from the tested optical modules, configure itself on the loopback mode and send the response message of the loopback configuration success to the tested optical modules through the in-band OAM channel. If the response message of the loopback configuration success from the tested optical modules is received by STRxs, STRxs can send the 10G/25G PRBS test data stream and receive the 10G/25G data stream from the tested optical modules.

trace: Test setup topology 1

text: 9 Xhaul Synchronization Testing
trace: 9 Xhaul Synchronization Testing

text: 9.1Synchronization test use cases, parameters and methodologies.
trace: 9.1Synchronization test use cases, parameters and methodologies.

text: This chapter delivers the testing methodologies, parameters and limits for PTP-based network technologies. The chapter is organized in different sections each representing a typical synchronization configuration mode. For each mode, all related metrics are identified, and limits are provided to deliver pass/fail verdicts.
trace: 9.1Synchronization test use cases, parameters and methodologies.
9.1Synchronization test use cases, parameters and methodologies.

text: Various synchronization options have been defined in the O-RAN WG4 CUS-Plane Specification \[2\] \(LLS- C1, LLS-C2, LLS-C3 and LLS-C4\). Depending on the specific O-RAN deployment being considered, not all of them might be relevant. When testing the S-Plane, the System Integrator shall identify which of the test cases are relevant depending on the specific deployment scenarios addressed. As a general guideline the following applies:

text: The Fronthaul focused tests for S-Plane for the current version of this specification covers LLS-C1, LLS-C2 and LLS-C3 using the ITU-T G.8275.1 \[5\] profile \(Full Timing Support\). Fronthaul focused tests for S-Plane for LLS-C1, LLS-C2 and LLS-C3 using the ITU-T G.8275.2 \[6\] profile \(Partial Timing Support\), and LLS-C4 are for future study.

text: The test cases apply to both lab and field deployment cases. For lab cases, the type and number of inserted Transport Node Elements \(TNE\) will be determined by operators \(or any other applicable end customer\). The tests are performed at Xhaul UNI interfaces, and not between individual TNEs. The Xhaul UNI interfaces include O-RU Fronthaul UNI, O-DU Fronthaul or Midhaul UNI.
trace: 9.1Synchronization test use cases, parameters and methodologies.
9.1Synchronization test use cases, parameters and methodologies.

text: The Test Topologies in all the test cases uses GNSS simulator to generate the GNSS signal to the network PRTC/T-GM. This high-quality reference from the simulator is used as the external reference for clock testers as well. The resultant accuracy of this method is a few nanoseconds. However, one can also use a GNSS signal feeding both the initial PRTC/T-GM in the network and the reference clock generating a 1pps/10MHz used to synchronize the clock testers for the measurements. Operator can make an allowance in this case, for all of the measurements for the accuracy of the reference. The magnitude of this allowance will depend on the specific GNSS reference in use.

- "1100ns time error" message from T-RC T-Tx to T-Tx, indicating a synchronization error measurement within the ORAN network

text: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: This chapter delivers the testing methodologies, parameters and performance limits for PTP-based network technologies in normal and fail-over or rearrangement scenarios of T-GM and TNEs across various network segments in the LLS-C3 configurations. The chapter is organized in different sections each representing a typical synchronization configuration mode. For each mode, all related metrics are identified, and limits are provided to deliver pass/fail verdicts.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: Various synchronization resiliency options have been defined in the O-RAN WG9 Synchronization Architecture and Solution Specification. Depending on the specific O-RAN deployment being considered, not all of them might be relevant. When testing the S-Plane, the System Integrator shall identify which of the test cases are relevant depending on the specific deployment scenarios addressed.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: Following high level options have been covered in this chapter and each of these options, clock advertisements and performance limits are discussed for normal and failover scenarios for T-GMs and TNEs in Backhaul, Midhaul and Fronthaul network segments in LLS-C3 configuration. Also scenarios like Asymmetry and Passive Port Monitoring are covered.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text:
* 1\. Ring topology in Midhaul and Backhaul \(LLS-C3 Configuration\)
  * a. O-DU connected to HSR and SYNC from Backhaul.
  * b. O-DU connected to HSR and SYNC from Backhaul. \(Aggregated Link\)
  * c. O-DU connected to CSR and SYNC from Backhaul.
  * 2\. Ring topology in Midhaul and Backhaul \(LLS-C3 Configuration\)
  * a. O-DU connected to HSR and SYNC from Midhaul.
  * b. O-DU connected to HSR and SYNC from Midhaul. \(Aggregated Link\)
  * c. O-DU connected to CSR and SYNC from Midhaul.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: It is important to note that, though Passive Port Monitoring is an OPTIONAL feature in ITU-T G.8275.1 ANNEX-G, if implemented, it is necessary for the equipment to conform to the requirement as per the specifications.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: For PTP rearrangement scenarios like member-link failover in Aggregated Ethernet Bundle and for other failover scenarios, operator can make choice based on the vendor TNE capability to estimate the end-to-end clock performance limit. However, the performance limits specified in this chapter applicable for both normal and rearrangement scenarios.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: The test cases apply to both lab and field deployment cases. For lab cases, the type and number of inserted Transport Node Elements \(TNE\) will be determined by operators \(or any other applicable end customer\). The tests are performed at Xhaul UNI interfaces, and not between individual TNEs. The Xhaul UNI interfaces include O-RU Fronthaul UNI, O-DU Fronthaul or Midhaul UNI.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: 1PPS test at O-RU UNI is typically used for debugging and monitoring the packet layer performance of the nearest TNE in the fronthaul. The intention of such test is that if the TNE vendor implemented the 1PPS interface, the 1PPS error measured on such interface at the O-RU UNI should be a reflection of the output time error of TNE. Operator shall pay attention to an unacceptably large deviation of 1PPS error, beyond the limits specified, which may indicate an incorrect behaviour of TNEs.

text: The Test Topologies in all the test cases uses GNSS simulator to generate the GNSS signal to the network PRTC/T-GM. This high-quality reference from the simulator is used as the external reference for clock testers as well. The resultant accuracy of this method is a few nanoseconds. However, one can also use a GNSS signal feeding both the initial PRTC/T-GM in the network and the reference clock generating a 1pps/10MHz used to synchronize the clock testers for the measurements. Operator can make an allowance in this case, for all of the measurements for the accuracy of the reference. The magnitude of this allowance will depend on the specific GNSS reference in use.
trace: 9.2Timing Solution & Resiliency in Ring Topology \(LLS-C3\)

text: For relative time error measurements at UNI \(e.g., O-RU Fronthaul UNI\) this document uses the metric max| 11 | \(1,2\) as defined in \[88\], Appendix XI. Please note this metric represents an estimation and the worst-case scenario. Tests that meet \(are below\) the limits are seen as PASS. Tests not meeting this metric may still be acceptable. The decision is for operators to make. However, if the measurement equipment support relative time error measurement, operator can use such equipment. Refer ITU-T G.8271.1 Appendix XI for more details.

description:
The diagram illustrates ORAN network elements arranged in two distinct rings – Ring22 Mid-haul and Ring1 Back-haul.

In Ring22 Mid-haul, there is interaction between T-GM1 (HSR) with HSR2, HSR3, and HSR4. T-GM1 emits a stateful (ST) message to all three HSR elements. Concurrently, CSR1 is transmits two messages labeled 'TR' and 'TT' towards O-DU1 through a bidirectional pathway. Additionally, CSR1 also sends two "ST" and "TT" messages to HSR3. HSR3 subsequently transmits its own "ST" and "TT" messages.

In Ring1 Back-haul, the interactions are between Br2, Br3, Br4, and Br5. Br2 exchanges "ST" and "TT" messages with Br1 (not shown but part of the backhaul structure), while Br3 and Br4 similarly exchange "ST" and "TT" with corresponding routers within the same back-haul ring.

text: Test Topology:
trace: 4 the preferred GM\) -->  --> Test Topology:

description:
The diagram illustrates the sequence of interactions in the ORAN (Open Radio Access Network) and 5G network architecture, highlighting the flow of messages between various components and time synchronization protocols:
1. "Clock Tester" sends "Frequency Reference Signal" from O-RU UNI (Out-Radio Unit Universal Interface) to HSR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC (High Speed Router Time-Clock/Time-Clock/eEPON)
2. HSR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC sends "Synchronization" towards O-DU1 T-TSC/eEEC and HSR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
3. HSR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC sends "1PPS Ref + 10MHz Ref" to BR1 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC and BR2 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
4. "Clock Tester" sends "Sync Message" from O-RU UNI to CSR1 T-BC/eEEC
5. CSR1 T-BC/eEEC sends "Sync Message" to HSR1 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
6. CSR1 T-BC/eEEC relays "Sync Message" from Clock Tester to HSR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC and HSR4 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
7. HSR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC provides "Frequency Reference Signal" to CSR2 T-BC/eEEC
8. CSR2 T-BC/eEEC sends "Sync Message" from Clock Tester to CSR1 T-BC/eEEC and GNS Sim T-GM2
9. GNS Sim T-GM2 receives "Sync Message" from CSR2 T-BC/eEEC and SR Message from O-DU2 T-TSC/eEEC, then sends "Sync Message" to O-DU2 T-TSC/eEEC
10. GNS Sim T-GM2 forwards "Sync Message" to BR6 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
11. BR4 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC provides "Frequency Reference Signal" to BR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
12. BR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC sends "Sync Message" to BR4 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
13. BR5 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC sends "Sync Message" from SR Message to BR3 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
14. BR5 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC sends "Sync Message" to HSR2 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC
15. BR5 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC sends "Sync Message" to O-DU2 T-TSC/eEEC
16. GNS Sim T-GM2 sends "Sync Message" to BR5 T-BC/T-TC/eEEC

text: This chapter specify a few additional use cases in LLS-C3 and LLS-C4 config models. Also LLS-C3 and LLS- C4 mixed configuration with and without GNSS assist and redundant T-GMs for co-located DUs and RUs are discussed. Each of these use cases are specified with performance limits and Pass/Fail verdict in normal and fail-over scenarios of GNSS and T-GM.

Depending on the specific O-RAN deployment being considered, not all of them might be relevant. When testing the S-Plane, the System Integrator shall identify which of the test cases are relevant depending on the specific deployment scenarios addressed.

text: O-RU UNI specified in the topology is for the network measurement. Two measurement planes have been specified in the document to cover all measurements. One at O-RU UNI for measuring X-haul network limits \(Packet + 1PPS\) and other at 1PPS measurement plane of O-RU to measure the 1PPS performance limits of O-RU in LLS-C4 configuration. Operator to position the Tester on these measurement planes for conducting the respective test.

text: The performance limits of O-RU in LLS-C4 when it is locked to local GNSS receiver has been specified in O- RAN.WG4.CUS documents. As per this specifications, the budget shall be based on ITU-T G.8272 \(PRTC class A, with max |TE|=100ns, or PRTC class B, with max |TE|=40ns on each GNSS receiver and max |TE|=30ns on O-RU. Max|TE| O-RU includes the O-RU clock recovery error from Local Time Source and any O-RU internal error. The LLS-C4 test cases in this section assumes the O-RU T-TSC Error of 10ns and O-RU internal Error of 20ns to arrive at the possible limits.

text: The test cases apply to both lab and field deployment cases. The test topologies in this test specification specify only few Transport Node Elements \(TNEs\) for illustration. However, for lab cases, the type and number of inserted Transport Node Elements \(TNE\) will be determined by operators \(or any other applicable end customer\) subject to the O-RU UNI limits. Some of the tests are performed at Xhaul UNI interfaces and some are at the O-RU 1PPS interfaces. The Xhaul UNI interfaces include O-RU Fronthaul UNI, O-DU Fronthaul or Midhaul UNI.
trace: config

text: 1PPS test at O-RU UNI is typically used for debugging and monitoring the packet layer performance of the nearest TNE in the fronthaul. The intention of such test is that if the TNE vendor implemented the 1PPS interface, the 1PPS error measured on such interface at the O-RU UNI should be a reflection of the output time error of TNE. Operator shall pay attention to an unacceptably large deviation of 1PPS error, beyond the limits specified, which may indicate an incorrect behaviour of TNEs.
trace: config

text: The Test Topologies in all the test cases uses GNSS simulator to generate the GNSS signal to the network PRTC/T-GM. This high-quality reference from the simulator is used as the external reference for clock testers as well. The resultant accuracy of this method is a few nanoseconds. However, one can also use a GNSS signal feeding both the initial PRTC/T-GM in the network and the reference clock generating a 1pps/10MHz used to synchronize the clock testers for the measurements. Operator can make an allowance in this case, for all of the measurements for the accuracy of the reference. The magnitude of this allowance will depend on the specific GNSS reference in use.
trace: config

text: For relative time error measurements at UNI \(e.g., O-RU Fronthaul UNI\) this document uses the metric max| | \(1,2\) as defined in \[88\], Appendix XI. Please note this metric represents an estimation and the worst-case scenario. Tests that meet \(are below\) the limits are seen as PASS. Tests not meeting this metric may still be acceptable. The decision is for operators to make. However, if the measurement equipment support relative time error measurement, operator can use such equipment. Refer ITU-T G.8271.1 Appendix XI for more details.
trace: config

text: For Frequency Limit at UNI \(e.g., O-RU Fronthaul UNI\) this document uses the metric defined as per WG4 section H.2 based on PRTC class for LLS-C3 configuration. Applicable MTIE limit shall apply for Frequency as per WG4 specification.

description:
The diagram illustrates interactions and connections within a system involving various components and testing setups:
1. "GNSS Frequency Reference" sent from Frequency Reference to GNSS Simulator
2. "1PPS Ref+10MHz Ref" sent from GNSS Simulator to T-GM
3. "PRTC-B, |TE|≤40ns" sent from T-GM to T-BC
4. Multiple T-BC instances labeled as T-BC/EEC/eECC send signals to multiple O-DU elements:
    - "T-BC/EEC/eECC" from T-BC to O-DU1 (twice: once between O-DU1 and T-TSC, and then from O-DU1 to Clock Tester)
    - similar messages sent to O-DU2
    - another instance of "T-BC/EEC/eECC" from T-BC to T-TSC
5. "T-TSC/EEC/eECC" signals from T-TSC to O-DU1
6. "T-TSC/EEC/eECC" signals from T-TSC to O-DU2
7. "T-TSC/EEC/eECC" signals from O-DU1 to T-BC
8. "T-TSC/EEC/eECC" signals sent from O-DU2 to multiple O-RU entities:
    - one instance to T-TSC, another to O-RU2 and O-RU1
9. "PRTC" sent from T-TSC to T-BC
10. "1PPS out" sent from CSR1 instances to the Clock Testers, with labels for different scenarios (For Regular R/F1) and Enhanced R/F1):
    - From T-TSC to CSR1 and multiple Clock Testers
    - From OCRG1 to CSR2 and multiple Clock Testers
11. "1PPS +10MHz" sent from multiple Clock Testers to either T-TSC/RRUUNI or T-GM
12. "O-DU UNIT" sent from clock testers to multiple O-DU and O-RU units

The diagram provides a comprehensive depiction of how signals and references are distributed within the system, emphasizing primary paths and alternate frequencies.

5This chapter specifies the test specification for a few use cases in LLS-C3 configurations for Shared O-RU.  
The test specification will address cases where two O-DUs connected to O-RUs \(Shared O-RUs\), via an  
Access Transport Networks \(TN\). On resiliency note, we are dealing with different elements \(such as T-GM

is considered as the 'ACTIVE' O-DU and other may be considered as the 'STANDBY' O-DU.

12It is also expected that an O-DU shall support multiple Shared O-RUs. For example, O-DU1 may be  
connected to O-RU1 and O-RU2; O-DU2 may also be connected to O-RU1 and O-RU2. If O-DU1 fails, both  
O-RUs switch to O-DU2.

shared with a single Operator, however one or more O-DUs are managed by more than one SROs. For the  
Shared O-RU with separate transport, the O-RU is configured to operate with more than one Shared  
Resource Operators O-DUs and the associated access TN.

each of SROs takes its own responsibility to the resiliency design to its transport network.

  * 11 PRTC/T-GM. This high-quality reference from the simulator is used as the external reference for clock
  * 12 testers as well. The resultant accuracy of this method is a few nanoseconds. However, one can also use a
  * 13 GNSS signal feeding both the initial PRTC/T-GM in the network and the reference clock generating a
  * 14 1pps/10MHz used to synchronize the clock testers for the measurements. Operator can make an allowance in
  * 15 this case, for all of the measurements for the accuracy of the reference. The magnitude of this allowance will
  * 16 depend on the specific GNSS reference in use.

  * 19 the worst-case scenario. Tests that meet \(are below\) the limits are seen as PASS. Tests not meeting this
  * 20 metric may still be acceptable. The decision is for operators to make. However, if the measurement
  * 21 equipment support relative time error measurement, operator can use such equipment. Refer ITU-T
  * 22 G.8271.1 Appendix XI for more details.

Test ID| SYNC.SE.01| Classification| Synchronization, Performance

Test Title| Pull-in/hold-in/pull-out limits on HSR/CSR  
Test Objective:| Verify the Pull-in/hold-in/pull-out range meets ITU-T
G.8262/G.8262.1  
Pre-Req| HSR/CSR connected to a tester which uses a stable reference clock  
Test Topology:| | |   
Test Configuration| | | To measure the 'pull-in' range, apply a high frequency offset to the selected clock  
input using clock tester so that the device will enter into holdover mode. Now
reduce  
the offset in arbitrary small step until EEC/eEEC locks to the input source.  
EEC/eEEC should lock to the input source before the offset reaches to ±4.6PPM.  
To measure the 'hold-in' range, vary the frequency offset arbitrarily, slowly,
and  
measure the highest frequency offset within which the device maintains lock.  
'Pull-out' range is the offset within which the device stays in locked state
and outside  
of which the device loses the lock irrespective of the rate of the frequency
change.  
Procedure:| Detailed Test procedure:| |   
| 1.  
Connect the tester to HSR/CSR fronthaul interface.| |   
| 2.| | Configure tester to provide the clock to DUT configured interface.  
| 3.  
Establish Frequency Synchronization on DUT.| |   
| 4.| | Inject PPM offset from the tester as per the ITU-T G.8262/G.8262.1  
| Verifications needed:| |   
| 1.  
Verify that SyncE and ESMC/eESMC are up.| |   
| 2.| | Perform the Pull-in/hold-in/Pull-out test on the device under test.  
| 3.  
Compare the test result as per ITU-T G.8262/G.8262.1| |   
Pass/Fail Criteria:| G.8262/ G.8262.1 clock specifications.| | Test shall pass if the measurement result is below the limit specified by ITU-T  
Test Output| ITU-T G.8262/G.8262.1 defined the limit of +/-4.6PPM| |

text: Test Topology: Test Configuration This section to be filled out when putting the test report \(may include device and/or tester configuration\) Procedure: Detailed Test procedure:  1\. Connect the tester to HSR/CSR fronthaul interface as per the Topology. 2. Configure tester as TimeTransmitter on the link1 and TimeReceiver on the link2. 3. Apply a stable time and frequency from the Tester to DUT input. 4. Establish Frequency and Phase Synchronization on DUT. 5. Perform the holdover test for duration of 1000 sec or more \(Stopping the PTP flows\) Verifications needed: 1\. Verify both frequency and phase lock on device under test \(HSR/CSR\) after stopping the PTP Flow, a. PTP should be in holdover state. b. Frequency should be in Locked state. 2. Verify the time error performance as per ITU-T G.8273.2 a. Frequency measurement should be as per ITU-T G.8262.1 eEEC. b. For enhanced TE specifications, the device conforms following Class-C specifications. 1. Maximum 2way absolute Time Error of 30 nsec. 2. Constant Time Error of +/-10 nsec. 3. Dynamic Time Error \(Filtered\) for low and high frequency 10 nsec and 30 nsec respectively. 4. Dynamic MTIE \(LF\) should be as per G.8273.2 mask. 3. Verify the MTIE mask defined as per ITU-T G.8273.2. NOTE: For TNEs doesn't support enhanced Class-C TE specifications shall support either Class-A or Class-B specifications as per ITU-T G.8273.2. Pass/Fail Criteria: Test shall pass if the measurement result is below the limit specified by ITU-T G.8273.2 clock specifications.
